text.title: 同一扇门前的两组人
text.situation:
一周后，两组人来使用同一个房间。几分钟内，前台变得压力很大：一位组织者指着邮件，另一位不停看时间。林没有立刻知道答案。她查看内部预约记录，请两位组织者等候，自己去找解决办法。

乔：你怎么设法这么快找到另一间房的？
林：我打电话给活动团队，他们知道一间小房间空着。
乔：你主动采取行动，没有等我。
林：我自己主动去查看房间，但改预约前先征求了意见。我们需要另一团队的合作。

致活动团队
谢谢帮助我们处理重复预约。两组人现在都在各自房间。请把今天的便条和预约记录放一起，便于了解错误是怎样发生的。

paragraphs.en: A week later, two groups arrived for the same room. Within a few minutes, Lin found herself in a high-pressure situation at the desk: one organiser was pointing at an email while another kept checking the time. Lin did not know the answer immediately. She checked the internal booking notes and asked both organisers to wait while she found a solution.

paragraphs.en:
Jo: How did you manage to find another room so quickly?
Lin: I called the events team. They knew a smaller room was free.
Jo: You took the initiative instead of waiting for me.
Lin: I checked the room on my own initiative, but I asked before changing the booking. We needed cooperation from the other team.

paragraphs.en:
To the events team
Thank you for helping us deal with the double booking. Both groups are now in their rooms. Please keep today’s note with the booking records so we can understand how the error happened.

S06.J06.P01.function: Two groups at the same door
S06.J06.P01.cue: 描述情况及林检查了什么。
acceptableAnswers: 那是压力很大的上午，林检查内部记录，设法找到了另一间房。

S06.J06.P02.function: Two groups at the same door
S06.J06.P02.cue: 说明林没有等乔就做了什么。
acceptableAnswers: 她率先处理问题，自己主动查看了一间房。

S06.J06.P03.function: Two groups at the same door
S06.J06.P03.cue: 说明另一团队为何重要。
acceptableAnswers: 他们的合作帮助两组人使用不同房间。

S06.J06.T01.function: Two groups at the same door
S06.J06.T01.cue: 社团忘记预约房间了。提出帮忙处理。
acceptableAnswers: 我可以帮你处理这个问题，让我给前台打电话。
